description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of different relational association categories evaluated in the MMRA benchmark, which assesses multi-granularity and multi-image relational reasoning in large visual language models. The chart is divided into ten distinct segments, each labeled with a category name, its corresponding count, and percentage of the total. The largest segment is “ObservationAngle” with 126 instances (12.28%), followed by “SimilarMaterial” with 106 (10.33%), and “SubEvent” with 100 (9.74%). Other categories include “UsageSimilarity” (100, 9.65%), “Environment” (90, 8.77%), “Layout” (90, 8.77%), “AppearanceSimilarity” (90, 8.77%), “SimilarEvent” (90, 8.77%), “MentalitySimilarity” (89, 8.67%), and “RelativePosition” (81, 7.90%). The smallest segment is “NearSameEntity” with 63 instances (6.34%). Each slice is color-coded and labeled directly on the chart with black text, and the percentages sum to approximately 100%, indicating a complete partition of the evaluated associations. The segments are arranged in descending order of size clockwise from the top-left, with “ObservationAngle” starting at the top-left and “NearSameEntity” at the top-center. No legend is present, as all labels are embedded within or adjacent to their respective slices.
